_comment: The marks an ordinary game offers, per command and argument, as a fixture.
Marks are live world state - what the player is looking at, holding, standing in - so no snapshot can be
taken from a running game the way data/values.json was. This file says what a player normally has: they are
somewhere, they own a property, an NPC is nearby, they are holding something. The mod filters the same list
by MarkKind and by whether each one currently resolves (NeedleTool.ResolvingMarks); this fixture is that
filter's answer for a plain moment in a plain save.
It exists so a declaration that depends on marks can be measured at all. Seven benchmark cases expect
`teleport #home`, and without this the model is never shown the word and cannot be scored on picking it.
A slot missing from this file is offered no marks, which is also what a command with no mark provider gets.
